solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dusty well cracked, life hard in the extreme

parts.note: a spring is a natural well, a source of water

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order
the extreme of the word hard is its very end, so only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A dried-up well has cracked open, and life at its harshest goes on around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' turns LIFE into FIEL, and 'in the extreme' takes the D at the end of 'hard'. 'Dusty' looks like a description of the well but is the first name of the British singer Dusty Springfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty Springfield was a celebrated British pop singer of the 1960s, so her first name leads to her surname.

clue.text: Lead sanctimonious bunch

parts.note: PI is short for pious, used of someone sanctimonious
a lot is a group or bunch of things

explanation.surface: A self-righteous group is put in charge of leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to guide or steer, which is to lead others along a route.

clue.text: Where a Yorkshireman needs his umbrella when under way?

definitions.text: Where a Yorkshireman needs his umbrella
definitions.meaning: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is clipped to t'
something under way is in progress, already started

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously shortens 'the' to t', so the dialect phrase for being out in the wet runs together into the same letters as the phrase for 'in progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan set in motion is said to be in train, an idiom for already happening or under way.

clue.text: Derrick's supporter mounting horse, on the go!

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the word for horse is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse
to have a go is to have a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone called Derrick is cheered on by a fan who climbs onto a horse and gallops off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derrick' looks like a man's name, but a derrick is a kind of crane.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a raised framework of girders that carries cranes, derricks or other lifting gear.

clue.text: Condition preventing one being out after dark?

definitions.text: Condition preventing one being out after dark?

parts.words: Condition preventing one being out after dark?
parts.note: being out here means being unconscious, asleep, not out on the town at night

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a curfew or a phobia keeping someone indoors at night; 'out' really means out cold, asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is a medical condition that stops a person dropping off at night.

clue.text: Youngster left on high peak — son's escaped

indicators.note: the son has got out of the mountain, so his letter is removed from it

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain peak

explanation.surface: A child is abandoned high on a mountain after the son of the party slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaped' removes the son's letter from the mountain. 'Youngster' suggests a child, but the young creature meant is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year is the specific animal sense of the youngster here.

clue.text: Bank holiday, Spain — the plane's heaving; it's difficult to move

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, was a British public holiday in late spring
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: heaving here means tossing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: On a holiday flight to Spain the packed plane lurches about, and moving around the cabin is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' rearranges THE PLANE. Whitsun, the Whit holiday, was formerly a British bank holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A costly possession nobody wants and nobody can get rid of is proverbially hard to offload.

clue.text: Champ getting to grips with algebraic characters oddly omitted four lines

indicators.note: to get to grips with is to grasp, so the word for champ holds the other letters

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters of the word algebraic leaves only its even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A champion wrestles with algebra, skipping odd symbols, then sets down a four-line verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters oddly omitted' keeps only the even-placed letters, and 'getting to grips with' puts them inside the chewing word, just after its first letter. 'Champ' looks like a winner but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic biographical poem invented by E. C. Bentley is a quatrain, a verse of exactly four lines.

clue.text: Fit American President: upfront, sharp, expensively kitted out

parts.note: to be fit is to be well, in good health

indicators.note: upfront asks for the letters at the front of the words American and President

parts.note: something sharp is pointed

explanation.surface: A healthy US president, frank and smartly dressed, is turned out in expensive clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-appointed house or room is lavishly furnished and equipped, so it is fitted out at expense.

clue.text: Composer has temperature following short vacation

indicators.note: following places the temperature letter after the vacation word

parts.note: hols is a British colloquial abbreviation of holidays

explanation.surface: A composer comes back from a short break with a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets suite.

clue.text: Dandy, 50, taking refuge in wicked Southern city

parts.note: Beau Nash was a famous 18th-century dandy of Bath society

indicators.note: the numeral hides inside the word for wicked, as if sheltering there

parts.note: vile means wicked, evil
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An elderly dandy of fifty hides out in some sinful Southern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash is the classic dandy of Georgian Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the state capital of Tennessee, a city of the American South.

clue.text: In retirement, Mrs Thatcher having to admit 'time is a four-letter word'

indicators.note: admitting lets the letter in, so it goes inside the turned name
retiring is going back, so the former prime minister's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was the British prime minister from 1979 to 1990

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, now retired, is forced to concede that 'time' has four letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns MARGARET round to TERAGRAM, and 'having to admit' slips T in to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra- is Greek for four, so a tetragram is any word written with four letters.

clue.text: Freud really missing regular letters from the country

indicators.note: taking out every other letter of the two words leaves the alternate ones that remain

explanation.surface: Freud is said to have lost some of his letters, sent from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing regular letters' drops F, E, D, E, L, Y to leave R, U, R, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Fur claimed with some hesitation?

parts.note: er is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating
saying 'mine' is claiming something as one's own

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a hesitant claim to a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts follow the order of speech: 'er' comes first, then the claim.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter coat of the stoat is a prized fur, used to trim royal and judicial robes.

clue.text: Dogs, mum's pets

parts.note: ma is a word for mum, and the possessive adds an S
a pet is a fit of sulking; tiffs are petty quarrels

explanation.surface: These dogs are Mum's beloved animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals but means sulks or huffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Large powerful guard dogs of an ancient breed are an example of the plural definition.

clue.text: Present awfully posh feature of museum?

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A very smart present sits in a museum display.
explanation.definitionFit: Most museums have a retail outlet near the exit selling souvenirs, so it is one of their usual features.

clue.text: Staff get tired hearing of election

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken

indicators.note: hearing of signals that the word for election is said aloud and replaced by a word with the same sound

parts.note: a poll is a vote or election

explanation.surface: Office workers grow weary listening to talk of an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a stick or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff can mean a pole or rod, as in the upright that carries a flag.

clue.text: Chill wind has Daisy sheltering in the city

indicators.note: the flower shelters inside the name of the city, so one sits within the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite
an aster is a flower of the daisy family

explanation.surface: A cold wind blows, and Daisy takes cover in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a girl's name but is the flower family.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a wind from the east blows off the continent and is notoriously cold.

clue.text: Drug problem involving king's personal servant?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the question word wraps round the royal letter

parts.note: a query is a question or problem
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A drugs scandal draws in the monarch's own attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the royal household attends personally on the sovereign, hence a personal servant of royalty.

clue.text: Band originally white hot, no longer 'with it'

indicators.note: in an original way, that is freshly arranged, so the letters are reordered
something no longer with us has gone, so the word it is taken out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock band was once red-hot but is now out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer with' takes IT out of WHITE to leave WHE, and 'originally' rearranges WHE with HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Who are an English rock group formed in the 1960s, famous for My Generation.

clue.text: Journalist witnessed item smuggled into prison?

parts.note: a hack is a slang word for a journalist
to witness something is to see it, past tense saw

explanation.surface: A reporter sees something being slipped into a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool for metal is the classic contraband hidden in a cake to saw through prison bars.

clue.text: A person of exceptional courage saving small girl

indicators.note: saving here means keeping, so the lion word holds the letter for small

parts.note: a lion is a very brave person

explanation.surface: A brave hero rescues a little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescue but tells you LION keeps S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a common female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Rebellion at the top reported in verse?

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the phrase is replaced by a word with the same sound

parts.note: a high coup is an uprising or putsch among those at the top

explanation.surface: News of a revolt among the leadership is told in poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines, an example of verse.

clue.text: Sitting inside drinking old chai naked? It could have its charms!

indicators.note: sitting inside means placed within the following words, so the answer lies hidden across them

explanation.surface: Someone sits indoors sipping old spiced tea without a stitch on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' is part of the hiding place, supplying the last letter, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm bracelet or necklace carries small trinkets, so a precious-metal link necklace can hold charms.

clue.text: Adult massage area in Caribbean location

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A grown-up massage parlour sits somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Aruba is a Dutch island in the southern Caribbean, off the coast of Venezuela.

clue.text: Evil location of 28's remote debts?

parts.note: the region named at 28 lies in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
remote means far away
IOUs are written promises to pay, i.e. debts

explanation.surface: The far-off debts of a north-eastern county are a wicked business.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across names a metropolitan county in North East England, so its location is NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal, an exact synonym of evil.

clue.text: Surf is finally up around Maine

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word is
around means turned round, so the little word up is reversed

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: The surf is finally up along the coast of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Spume is the foam or froth on breaking waves, much the same as surf.

clue.text: Riverside communities want year-end reforms

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters are reshaped into new words

explanation.surface: Towns along a river are pressing for change at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like the communities' demand but rearranges WANT YEAR-END. It is a metropolitan county in North East England around Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: The county is named for its two rivers and is made up of the towns along their banks.
